# Remove All Adjacent Duplicates In String.

@example Cutting the first "ss" brings two i's together; cutting those, then "ss", then "pp", then the last two i's leaves only the m.
"mississippi"
=> "m"

@example No two neighbouring letters are the same, so nothing is cut.
"level"
=> "level"

@example Cutting "oo" brings the two n's together, and they go too.
"noon"
=> ""

# A single letter.
"z"
=> "z"

# Two letters: the same, and different.
"qq"
=> ""

"pq"
=> "pq"

# Three equal letters in a row keep one, four keep none, five keep one.
"aaa"
=> "a"

"bbbb"
=> ""

"xaaaaay"
=> "xay"

# Each cut brings two equal letters together, three times over. Cutting
# every twin pair once and stopping would leave "abccbx".
"abcddcbx"
=> "ax"

# After "rr" is cut, the letters before and after it meet as "qq" and go
# too: a pass that skips each pair without looking back would keep "pqqs".
"pqrrqs"
=> "ps"

# Twin pairs at the very start and the very end.
"ccdeff"
=> "de"

# Every letter once: nothing to cut.
"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
=> "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"

# 300 letters, "ab" repeated, with no twin pair: all of them remain.
""
=> ""

# "ab" repeated 2500 times, then "ba" 2500 times (10^4 letters): at each
# step the only twin pair is in the middle, so up to 5000 letters wait on
# a stack at once (a fixed stack of 4096 overflows), and in the end
# nothing remains.
""
=> ""

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them). Full-size
# cases, 10^5 letters, come with milestone M7.
@gen 1 small
"aabbabbbb"
=> "a"

@gen 2 small
"cbccaaa"
=> "cba"

@gen 3 small
"bccbcbccb"
=> "c"

@gen 4 small
"abaa"
=> "ab"

@gen 5 small
"bbbaabaaba"
=> "ba"

@gen 8 small
"baccaca"
=> "bca"

@gen 10 small
"abaaabbb"
=> "abab"
